name: Musée Honmè (Palais Royal de Hogbonou)
subtitle: Historic palace of the kings of Porto-Novo preserving royal courtyards, altars, and the diplomatic legacy of King Toffa I.

facts.label: Original name
facts.value: Honmè ('inside the palace' in the Gun language)

facts.label: Layout
facts.value: Traditional earthen compound with multiple shaded courtyards, ceremonial halls, and ancestral tombs

parts.text: The ancestral royal palace of the kingdom of Hogbonou, transformed into a national museum in downtown Porto-Novo. Known locally as Honmè ('inside the home'), this sprawling mudbrick palace compound illustrates the living court traditions of the Gun royalty. Visitors walk through labyrinthine interior courtyards, reception halls where King Toffa I received European envoys, ceremonial royal carriages, ancestral shrines, and rooms documenting the complex court etiquette of queens and high dignitaries.

gaps: Digital archives of royal diplomatic correspondence between King Toffa and French authorities are held in overseas archives.
